key_insight: Coarse-mesh graph neural networks predict sparse flow observables without reconstructing the full state, matching or outperforming finer-mesh surrogates at lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers efficient prediction of probe signals and integrated quantities for flow monitoring, system identification, and state estimation.
method: Train GNN surrogates directly on coarse meshes to predict selected observables.
Adapt parameter sampling using changes in flow frequency spectra.
Use noise-augmented, multi-step unrolled training to improve long-horizon autoregressive predictions.
evidence_signal: Tests on parameterized 2D/3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity showed generalization to unseen conditions; adaptive sampling reduced maximum errors by an order of magnitude versus uniform sampling.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the tested geometries and Reynolds/Rayleigh-number ranges remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks
